reports.title: Scott McGlinchey's Fishing Report
reports.text:
As water temperatures continue to cool, the bass fishing on Kentucky Lake has really improved. We're now catching more quality bass, and it's becoming increasingly common to catch bigger fish than smaller ones.
The topwater bass bite started in late July and has continued right through the summer and into the fall. During August and early September, we caught good numbers of bass, with several different locations producing schooling fish on and off throughout the day.
We're now catching considerably more keeper-size bass, and the quality of the fish has improved dramatically. I've had several days when we've literally lost count of the number of keeper bass we've caught, with some outings…

reports.title: Anglers Enjoy Marathon of Great Weather
reports.text:
Light winds teamed up with mild temperatures to provide excellent fishing conditions for bass and crappie anglers as October faded away and passed the torch on to November.
Crappie fishing has been good lately and some hefty stringers have been taken. Depths of 12 to 15 feet were producing but several anglers have reported success from the 9 to 12 foot range at times. Up Big Sandy and into West Sandy some crappie have been caught in 6 to 8 foot depths at times. However, the shallow bite has been slow to get going this fall as most fish are opting to hold out a bit deeper. A few cloudy rainy days would likely stimulate more crappie to move up to shallower depths as would lower surface temps…
